create.title: Exact complete-Mobius recombination of the D=1 squarefree survivor
create.statement_tex: Let R=X^(1/4), N=floor(X), 1<<M<=R^2, J=M^(3/4), S=ceil(M^(1/4)), and let F_U(n)=1_(n odd)1_(|k(n)^2-Nn|>J)chi_4(n)n^(-3/4)A_U(n)e(sqrt(Nn)) retain the literal zero-extended actual profile, endpoints, nearest-integer convention, and strict mask. The Round-152 survivor satisfies P_U^*=sum_(s<S odd)sum_(tau odd)mu^2(tau)F_U(tau s^2). Complete inversion mu^2(tau)=sum_(a^2|tau)mu(a), tau=a^2b, and r=as give P_U^*=sum_(r odd)C_S(r)sum_(b odd)F_U(r^2b), where C_S(r)=sum_(a|r,r/a<S)mu(a). For r<S, C_S(r)=1_(r=1). For r>=S, |C_S(r)|<=d(r), r^2b asymp M, and the actual M^(-3/4) weight give an absolute boundary O_epsilon((M^(-1/4)+M^(1/4)/S)X^epsilon)=O_epsilon(X^epsilon). Hence P_U^*=sum_(b odd)F_U(b)+O_epsilon(X^epsilon)=P_U+O_epsilon(X^epsilon), using the accepted Round-152 exact-, small-defect-, and large-square-factor owners. Thus complete Mobius inversion followed by complete recombination self-returns to the original direct large-defect wave; the artificial a- and s-blocks are not independent owners. This does not rule out a future coefficient-sensitive signed bilinear theorem, gives no new range, and proves no downstream theorem or exponent.

update.statement_tex: Round 151 leaves a low-two-adic h|g recovery fibre outside its recombined row corridors; for D>1 this coefficient-sensitive collar and the generic complement remain open. At D=d=L=1 the boundary-complete transform gives the actual square-root wave P_U. Round 152 proves the strict range M^449>>R^780 and the exact decomposition P_U=P_U^*+O_epsilon(X^epsilon), with exact squares, small nonzero defects, and large square factors target-safe. Round 153 proves that complete squarefree Mobius inversion of P_U^*, followed by r=as recombination, has coefficient C_S(r)=sum_(a|r,r/a<S)mu(a), equals 1_(r=1) for r<S, and has an O_epsilon(X^epsilon) r>=S boundary. It therefore returns the direct large-defect wave and supplies no independent Type-I/Type-II owner or new range. The s=1 layer and the full direct large-defect wave remain open below M^449 asymp R^780. This is a scoped proof frontier, not a lower bound or an impossibility theorem for future signed methods.

reject.reason: Exact r=as recombination gives C_S(r)=1_(r=1) for r<S and an absolutely safe r>=S boundary, so the complete expansion returns the direct wave rather than creating independent saved blocks.
For 1<r<S the required cancellation occurs between different a- and s-preimages of the same r; separate ownership destroys this exact divisor sum.
The compulsory a=s=1 seam has coefficient one and is exactly the returned direct large-defect wave.
The diagonal and pigeonhole quantities are upper capacities for coefficient-blind majorants; surviving Mobius and chi_4 signs can cancel.
Round 152 permits scalar-level removal before Cauchy, with divisor-bounded expanded multiplicity, but deleting summands inside a signed masked correlation is invalid.
For the relevant pair, 1-2lambda+2kappa=123/398>0, and absolute s-block summation gives (AS_0)^(123/398).
That figure grants quadratic spacing to all ambient B points; a literal fixed-q fibre has only O(sqrt(B/q)+1) points.
The literal profile and mask may vanish on ambient points and depend on the expansion variables, so ambient capacity does not force actual signed occupancy.
The equality a_1^2b_1=a_2^2b_2 parametrizes a product fibre that is not generally an exact Nn square and must retain its Mobius coefficient.
The actual A_U(a^2bs^2) and defect mask couple the separated source variables; no direct theorem specialization exists.
The audit covers a specified corpus and direct translations only; it neither rules out other sources nor a new signed argument.
R^(1/2)M^(-1/4) is the size of a positive term on the printed upper-bound right-hand side, not a lower bound for the actual sum.
Its complete actual-weight absolute mass is O_epsilon((M^(-1/4)+M^(1/4)/S)X^epsilon)=O_epsilon(X^epsilon).
The collapse only shows what happens after complete recombination; a signed cross-block theorem remains logically possible and would also prove the direct wave.
The s=1 layer is compulsory and useful, but the remaining 1<s<S layers require their own owner unless a complete signed argument treats them.
The exact identity gives no estimate for the returned direct wave below M^449 asymp R^780 and treats only one D=d=L=1, t=1 route.
Those owners have distinct coefficients, fibres, profiles, and endpoint interfaces and were not part of the Round-153 identity.

round_assessment.reason: Round 153 proves an exact all-scale algebraic self-collapse for the proposed complete squarefree-Mobius route, reconciles the mask and compulsory short-divisor seams, corrects the bilinear power and spacing interpretations, and source-audits the closest direct theorems.
